speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens when you wake up frightened—do you seem fully awake and able to answer questions, or do you appear confused and hard to rouse?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: It sounds like she is fully awake and aware during these episodes, which helps distinguish this from sleep terrors. Does she report having specific, frightening dreams before she wakes up, or does the fear come out of nowhere without a clear narrative?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: She recalls bad dreams and exhibits bedtime procrastination, which strongly points toward nightmares rather than sleep terrors. I will request a standard sleep study to rule out any underlying sleep-disordered breathing or other physiological causes. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
